messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates Java code to GNU C++11 code. The code should reads and writes I/O from the console.

samples.content:
<translation>

#include <bits/stdc++.h>

using namespace std;

#define endl "\n"

using ll = long long;

const ll INF = 1e18 + 1;

const int N = 103;

string getStr () {
    string str;
    getline(cin, str);
    return str;
}

char getChar () {
    char ch;
    cin >> ch;
    return ch;
}

int getDigit() {
    int digit;
    cin >> digit;
    return digit;
}

vector<int> getV (int n) {
    vector<int> vec (n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        cin >> vec[i];
    }
    return vec;
}

int main() {
    int n, K;
    cin >> n >> K;
    int cnt1 = 0, cnt2 = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        char ch;
        cin >> ch;
        if (ch == '50')
            cnt1++;
        else
            cnt2++;
    }

    vector<ll> nCr (N, vector<ll> (N, 0));
    nCr[0][0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i < N; i++) {
        nCr[i][0] = 1;
        for (int j = 1; j <= i; j++) {
            if (j == 0 || j == i)
                nCr[i][j] = 1;
            else
                nCr[i][j] = (nCr[i - 1][j] + nCr[i - 1][j - 1]) % INF;
        }
    }

    ll **dist;
    ll **dp;
    dist = new ll *[203];
    dp = new ll *[203];
    for (int i = 0; i < 203; i++) {
        dist[i] = new ll[203];
        dp[i] = new ll [203];
        for (int j = 0; j < 203; j++) {
            dist[i][j] = INF;
        }
    }

    vector <pair<ll, Wedge>> pq;
    dist[0][0][0] = 0;
    dp[0][0][0] = 1;
    pq.push_back({0, {0, 0, 0}});
    while (!pq.empty()) {
        auto curr = pq.back();
        pq.pop_back();
        ll d = curr.first;
        int x = curr.second.first;
        int y = curr.second.second;
        int z = curr.second.third;
        if (z == 0) {
            int rem_x = cnt1 - x;
            int rem_y = cnt2 - y;
            for (int i = 0; i <= rem_x; i++) {
                for (int j = 0; j <= rem_y; j++) {
                    if (i + j == 0)
                        continue;

                    if (i * 50 + j * 100 > K)
                        break;

                    if (dist[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1] >= d + 1) {
                        if (dist[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1] > d + 1) {
                            dist[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1] = d + 1;
                            pq.push_back({dist[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1], {i + x, j + y, z ^ 1}});
                            dp[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1] += dp[x][y][z] * nCr[rem_x][i] % INF * nCr[rem_y][j] % INF;
                            dp[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1] %= INF;
                        }
                        else {
                            dp[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1] += dp[x][y][z] * nCr[rem_x][i] % INF * nCr[rem_y][j] % INF;
                            dp[i + x][j + y][z ^ 1] %= INF;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        else {
            int rem_x = x;
            int rem_y = y;
            for (int i = 0; i <= rem_x; i++) {
                for (int j = 0; j <= rem_y; j++) {
                    if (i + j == 0)
                        continue;

                    if (i * 50 + j * 100 > K)
                        break;

                    if (dist[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1] >= d + 1) {
                        if (dist[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1] > d + 1) {
                            dist[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1] = d + 1;
                            pq.push_back({dist[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1], {x - i, y - j, z ^ 1}});
                            dp[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1] += dp[x][y][z] * nCr[rem_x][i] % INF * nCr[rem_y][j] % INF;
                            dp[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1] %= INF;
                        }
                        else {
                            dp[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1] += dp[x][y][z] * nCr[rem_x][i] % INF * nCr[rem_y][j] % INF;
                            dp[x - i][y - j][z ^ 1] %= INF;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if (dist[cnt1][cnt2][1] == INF)
        cout << -1;
    else
        cout << dist[cnt1][cnt2][1];
    cout << " " << dp[cnt1][cnt2][1] << endl;

    return 0;
}

Note that GNU C++11 uses `#include <bits/stdc++.h>` to include all standard library headers, while the original Java 8 code does not require any explicit header includes. The `vector` class in GNU C++11 is used to replace Java's `List` class for dynamic array storage. The `ll` typedef is used to represent long long integers, similar to Java's `long` data type. 

Also note that `std::string getStr()` function is used to get a line from standard input, which is similar to Java's `getLine` function in `InputReader` class. The `getStack` function in Java is not directly translated to the GNU C++11 code, as a similar data structure is not directly available. 

However, a priority queue data structure (using `std::priority_queue` in GNU C++11) can be used to achieve the same functionality as Java's `ArrayDeque` class. 

Also note that `Tuple` class in the original Java code is translated into a custom `Wedge` struct in the GNU C++11 code for better readability. 

The mixed-model usage of `sin>>Digit_At_A_Time` and `getline(getstringAt_A_Time)` input statements which are generally generally clear an inconsistent is ungecommon. Because you input 'Digit_At_A_Time for 'n' and 'K', while everything else is got in vaugle lines thru getline(cin,str).
